mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across monetary policy regimes.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no significant correlation with 20-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the direction of the relationship reverses in more than 40% of the sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8.0% indicates severe economic weakness, which depresses near-term corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.0% occurs in more than 60% of instances with negative 20-day returns, but the return direction is positive in more than 40% of such triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return difference).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a broad-based deterioration in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS occurs in more than 50% of instances, but the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of these cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return difference).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO growth rate < 0), the market anticipates reduced corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth rate < 0 occurs in more than 50% of instances, but the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of these cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return difference).

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly GDP growth rate (derived from GDPC1) signals strong economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days (approximately one quarter).
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate shows no significant correlation with 60-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the direction of the relationship reverses in more than 40% of the sample.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% annually signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% occurs in more than 60% of instances with negative 20-day returns, but the return direction is positive in more than 40% of such triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return difference).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strong job growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) and weak housing starts (HOUST growth < 0.5%) indicate a labor market overheating without broad-based demand, which triggers Federal Reserve tightening expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and HOUST growth < 0.5% occurs in more than 50% of instances, but the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of these cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return difference).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month signals aggressive monetary tightening, which immediately pressures equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS change > 0.25% occurs in more than 50% of instances, but the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of these cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return difference).
